findings.reason: the sentence belongs in the node brief, not the plan, and as written it sends a node to build a selector and rewrite evidence scripts for scoping that `sn run --focus <manifest>` already provides.
findings.text: the new parenthetical "if a source selector is added to sn run for this, it replaces the ad hoc source-id lists in the evidence scripts" prescribes implementation. A section is not to name a code path, a step sequence, or a function to extend, and this one does all three: it names a CLI command to modify, the code change (adding a selector), and a downstream refactor of the evidence scripts. It is also conditionally stated, so it never says whether the selector is required, and the premise is contradicted by the tool: `sn run --focus` already accepts a `sn-sources` manifest and expands it to focus paths (imas_codex/cli/sn.py:1498-1512), which is exactly the source scoping §4 needs. A worker dispatched from this text must first test the plan's guess against the code, and the review round is spent there instead of on the run

findings.reason: §5's plan of record depends on a reserve §4 does not compute, and the fix is one subtraction in §4's limit or a corrected §5 claim.
findings.text: §4's cost limit is "the USD 350 approval's remaining balance less the unspent part of the USD 60 tranche authorised to sn-catalog-consistency §2", while the plan's new §5 (line 66) states "§4's limit reserves the unspent part of that ceiling", its own documentation ceiling of measured rate times backlog. §4's stated formula contains no such reserve, so the two claims cannot both hold: a coordinator sizing to §4's limit as written may spend the whole remaining balance and leave §5 unfunded, while §5 reads in good faith as though it were protected. Before this round §4 had no reserve at all and the objection was about draws on the approval; the reserve mechanism was added for sn-catalog-consistency and not extended to the section the same edit introduced

findings.reason: a coordinator dispatching from the table can start §5 beside §4 and make §4's done-when unreachable, so §5's depends-on needs s4 (or the window needs an explicit precedence rule).
findings.text: §4's new census clause requires that "the census, the accepted count and the guard readings below come from one reading taken after the run ends, with no graph writer running, and are recorded together", but the plan's dependency table (line 22) gives §5 depends-on sn-integrity-backlog#s52 only, and followup f-sfdc-001 (line 72) likewise starts §5 as soon as no §52 run is writing — so §5, which writes documentation to the graph, may legally be mid-run when §4 takes its single reading. The two sections are then unsatisfiable together: §4's gate cannot be met while §5 writes, and nothing orders §5 after §4

response_events.note: The selector parenthetical is removed; §4 keeps only 'scoped by source', which sn run --focus with a source manifest already provides, and the brief says so.
§4's limit now also reserves the unspent part of §5's documentation ceiling.
§5 now waits on §4, so no documentation write overlaps §4's single post-run reading.
